summary: Ludwig Sütterlin was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and Heidelberg University under Hermann Osthoff, earning his Ph.D. He taught at Heidelberg University (PD in 1890, associate professor 1896–1913) and held a chair at the University of Freiburg (1913–1924).

Philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein studied at institutions including the Technische Hochschule Berlin, Owens College, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge (Ph.D. c. 1929). He held posts at Trinity College, Cambridge (1929–1947) and the University of Cambridge (1930–1947).

Indologist Ludwik Skurzak studied at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Collège de France, and with Louis Renou, Jean Przyluski, Jules Bloch, Stanisław Schayer, and Helena Willman-Grabowska. He was a professor at Breslau (1945–1978).

Indologist Ludwik Sternbach studied at Lviv and Jagiellonian University under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak and Helena Willman-Grabowska. He held posts at Jagiellonian (1933–1938), Lviv (1939–1941), Mumbai (1944), Sorbonne Nouvelle (1970–1972), and Collège de France (1972–1976).

Linguist and Indologist Luigi Heilmann studied at Padua under Luigi Suali and Ambrogio Ballini, and later at Bologna. He held posts at Università Cattolica (1934–1937), Pavia (c. 1953–1956), Cagliari (1955–1956), and Bologna as professor of linguistics (c. 1956–1981).
Luigi Pio Tessitori was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Paolo Emilio Pavolini at the University of Florence from c. 1906 to 1910, completing his dissertation there.

Luigi Suali worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Bologna under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Bologna (1907) and the University of Pavia (acting professor 1909–1910; ordinary professor 1914–1956).

Luigia Nitti-Dolci was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Theodor Bloch, receiving her doctorate from the University of Paris by 1938. She served as editor of Nepalese manuscripts at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne.

Luis Oscar Gómez worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from Puerto Rico, Yale under Stanley Insler, and Michigan. He held major posts at the University of Michigan, including department chair (1986) and Arthur F. Thurnau Professor (1997).

Linguist and Indologist Luise Hercus studied at St Anne's College, Tollington School, and the Australian National University. She held posts at St Anne's College (1948–1954), the University of Adelaide (1965–1969), and the Australian National University (c. 1969–1991).
Indologist Luise Hilgenberg studied at the University of Bonn, earning a Dr.med. by 1922 and a Dr. phil. by 1933 under doctoral supervisor Willibald Kirfel.

Lumír Jisl, a scholar of archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Charles University (1940–1949). He served as secretary at the CAS Institute of Archaeology in Prague (1956) and as Privatdozent at Charles University (1960).
Lungten Dubgyur works in Tibetology and other fields. He earned a graduate degree from Sherubtse College, an LL.B. from Government Law College, Mumbai, and an LL.M. from the University of Edinburgh.

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima, a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot starting in 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Sinologist Lutz Bieg earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University (1971) and his Habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin (1986). From 1989 to 2008, he served as ordinary professor of Chinese studies, literature, and philosophy at the University of Cologne.
Lyne Bansat-Boudon is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Armand Minard and Marie-Claude Porcher.

Lynette Monteiro, active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earned her Ph.D. from the University of Ottawa (1986–1996). She held posts at Sea Glass Psychological Services (1997) and the Ottawa Mindfulness Clinic as Director of Professional Training (2003).

Sinologist and historian Lynn Struve studied at the University of Washington (c. 1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (c. 1967–1974). She held a post at Indiana University Bloomington around 1977.

Lynn Teskey Denton, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, earned degrees from McMaster University (B.A. 1972) and Somerville College (B.Litt. 1973–1975). She taught at McMaster University and was an assistant professor at Concordia University (1984–1989).
